newsitem.title: FRANCE: French domestic wheat firm on exports, weather.
newsitem.headline: French domestic wheat firm on exports, weather.

text.p: French wheat prices stayed mostly firm on Thursday as export demand underpinned the old crop and dry weather raised further fears over yields from the new crop, traders said.
There was little actual businness however ahead of this afternoon's European Union export tender, while barley prices paused after a recent rally and maize rose on the back of firm bids for wheat.
"The situation is clear; either buyers pay up or they can choose to wait," said one operator commenting on the strength in wheat.
Rouen-delivered wheat, which traded at 910 francs per tonne on Wednesday, was bid at 905 francs to 910 francs for April depending on silo and 900-905 francs for May excluding carry.
New-crop buyers were at 910 francs for August or 905 for delivery spread over four months from September.
One trader noted new export business was coming through regularly, putting downward pressure on stock forecasts, while the only moisture reaching new crops was the "morning dew."
Algeria earlier bought 100,000 tonnes of May/June wheat , possibly French, at $183-184 including freight, traders said.
Several EU wheat or flour tenders for food aid are in progress, they added.
MATIF fob barge wheat futures were up one franc for May at 945 francs and up four for September at 916 on total volume of 78 lots.
Cash barley was quoted at 870 francs per tonne for April/May at Rouen, but with a firmer bias in the wake of Wednesday's sale of optional-origin barley to Saudi Arabia.
Fob Atlantic maize was pegged at 900 francs per tonne for the same period, up around 10 francs since early this week.
New-crop maize for October-December was nominally worth 950 francs per tonne, up five francs, traders said.
